items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: we were talking about Lionel Hampton and how these guys, when they get to their instrument, you had to help him up on stage but when he gets to the instruments he feels no pain and he’s playing.

ctx.x: You know you made a comment when you came in today and our professor who brought you over, and you said something like, “I want to be like you when I grow up.” And I’m wondering if this music keeps you young.

Oh yeah. You know we just had this conversation and, back at the room over there at the hotel this morning. Because we were talking about Lionel Hampton and how these guys, when they get to their instrument, you had to help him up on stage but when he gets to the instruments he feels no pain and he’s playing. There was another guy that Cascadu mentioned. Then I mentioned Candido, 98 years old and he’s still playing. He wears a brace for his arthritis in the back. He can’t stand up. He leans on the drum. They put…
And they learned to play within, like if they lost their high notes they learned to play without them.
